messages:
alex: noticed a latency spike on prod inference around 10:43 UTC, p50 jumped from 45ms -> 150ms on r5-gpu-4 nodes. graph shows token service widening tail.

maya: saw the alert, digging into traces now. is this correlated with the triton rollout?

ravi: yes, we rolled Triton 2.1.4 at 10:30 canary -> 10:40 full. can confirm increased kernel launch times in traces.

alex: attaching quick flame: `nvprof` sample shows attention kernel launch overhead increased ~3x; also more host<->device memcpy spikes.

maya: profiler snapshot:
```
# summary from perf run
Kernel: fast_attention_forward (was Flash-attn plugin)
avg launch latency: 12us -> 40us
avg compute: unchanged
overall token latency: +2.8x
```

maya: also noticed KV cache miss ratio up from 0.4% -> 6% for long-chat workloads. that could be causing extra recompute of prefixes.

tomas: KV eviction pattern looks weird. runtime GC triggered more frequently after the Triton change? I see a new allocator hook in commit `a7b3fc2` that touched KV lifetime.

sam: can someone paste the kernel selection logs? we log selector decisions at debug level.

alex: pasted subset:
```
[kernel-selector] model=redwood-v1 seq=1024 hw=cuda_80 selected=generic_attention_tiled reason=fallback-compat
[kernel-selector] model=redwood-v1 seq=256 hw=cuda_80 selected=fast_attention_plugin reason=optimal
```
Weird that long sequences are falling back to generic when before they hit fast plugin.

ravi: hypothesis: Triton change altered shared memory availability or sm occupancy heuristics, so selector's microbench marks now prefer generic for long sequences because our cost model is skewed.

maya: repro on staging: roll back to Triton 2.1.3 -> selector picks fast plugin again and p50 returns to baseline. confirming regression.

infra-bot: deploy rollback to canary initiated by @ravi at 10:58 UTC.

alex: workaround: we can force override selector for affected models in config: `kernel_selector.forced_plugins = {redwood-v1: fast_attention_plugin}` — should be safe for canary. Doing that now on canary pool.

ops-bot: throttle rule applied: cap qps to 60% for long-seq routes to reduce compounding during rollback.

tomas: digging deeper: the allocator change added `cudaMemPoolTrim` calls on eviction that increase device-side stalls under contention. That explains the memcpy spikes and KV GC increase.

maya: action items:
- short term: keep selector override + rollback Triton to 2.1.3 on remaining nodes (ravi/ops).
- medium: adjust cost model inputs to re-run microbenchmarks under current driver to avoid misclassifying plugins (tomas + alex).
- long term: add integration test that runs KV-heavy chat workloads under new triton/driver permutations (maya + eng-ml).

ravi: rolling Triton back on remaining pools now. will follow up when done.

alex: logging note: add a diagnostic tag to kernel selection decisions so we can correlate `kv_miss_rate` and `mem_pool_trim` calls in the future.

maya: thanks all. will file a short postmortem and link perf artifacts (nvprof traces, selector logs, commit ids).

sam: thumbs up. -- please ping if rollback doesn't fully restore tail.

ravi: rollback complete on all prod GPU pools at 11:08 UTC, p50 back to ~47ms, tail improved. will keep watch for 1 hour.

maya: opened INC-2026-452 in incident tracker and attached traces + recommended follow-ups.

alex: saved selector override as temp config: `rb-1763004321-force-fast-attn` (expire 24h).

meya: (typo) meant maya. :sweat_smile:
